question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{bmatrix}$, then $A^{3}$ is:
explanation:
Step 1 Identify the specific matrix structure given in the prompt. The matrix $A$ has non-zero values exclusively along its main diagonal, and since these elements are all equal to 5, it is a scalar matrix. We can factor out the scalar 5 to express it in terms of the identity matrix $I$: $A = 5I$.

Step 2 Compute the third power of the matrix using our algebraic expression: $A^3 = (5I)^3 = 5^3 \cdot I^3$. Since multiplying the identity matrix by itself any number of times always yields the identity matrix ($I^3 = I$), this simplifies directly to $125I$.

Step 3 Expand the expression back into its explicit matrix format by multiplying every diagonal element of the identity matrix by 125: $125I = \begin{bmatrix}125 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 125 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 125\end{bmatrix}$. This corresponds exactly to option B.
